  "text": "Every Tuesday, Martin put a blue cup beside the library kettle. The other cups were white, with the council crest fading in the wash.

“Who’s that one for?” asked Leena, on her first afternoon.

“Mrs Vale. She brings the newspapers back.”

“I thought newspapers stayed here.”

“They do now.”

At eleven, a woman in a green coat appeared carrying a bundle tied with string. Martin filled the blue cup without asking.

Mrs Vale sat near the radiator and untied the bundle. Inside were last week’s papers, each folded to the crossword.

“Seven down was wrong,” she said.

“The clue or your answer?”

She gave him a look.

In November, the council removed the kettle. A notice explained that refreshments were available from the machine in the entrance hall.

Mrs Vale studied the buttons.

“It wants a pound.”

“Yes,” said Leena.

“For that little cup.”

“Yes.”

She returned to the radiator with her coat still buttoned.

The following Tuesday, Leena brought a flask. She poured tea into the blue cup beneath the desk, beside the returned books.

Martin watched her.

“That’s your own tea.”

“I made too much.”

By January, there were three flasks under the desk. Nobody discussed them.

One Tuesday, Mrs Vale arrived without the newspapers.

“Forgotten something?” Martin asked.

“Apparently.”

She stood with her hands resting on her empty shopping bag.

Leena fetched the blue cup.

“We’ve got today’s,” she said, pulling out a chair.

Mrs Vale took off her coat. While the tea cooled, Martin found a pencil and rubbed out the answer he had written at seven down."
